utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please be so kind to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I think, Mr. Stamp, the order of this week is that we first start with one viva voce witness, and it's the last one that was still waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President, and that is Witness P.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's Witness P. And for Witness P, has, of course, a pseudonym and facial distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning. Just one simple point relating to the intervention of Mr. Ierace on last Thursday. We had agreed that the Defence would be given the opportunity to state its opinion at the end of this hearing today, Monday, in order to save time. Mr. Ierace mentioned a certain number of military references, and I don't know whether Mr. Stamp can tell us as early as now what brigades, corps, and battalions precisely Mr. Ierace was referring to last Thursday. Can Mr. Stamp tell us which units we are talking about, or rather Mr. Ierace was talking about, so that we can better prepare our response. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like him to do it now in open court or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think Mr. Stamp -- that is, I hope that Mr. Stamp can do it now. But -- well, he can do it whenever he chooses to do so, but I hope he'll be able to respond now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With respect to my friend, Mr. Ierace will be here today. He is prepared to respond -- to follow up on all submissions that he made to the Court. But having regard to what is happening in Sarajevo and the direction of the Court in respect of this witness, I respectfully ask if we could complete this witness as quickly as possible, and hear the witnesses on videolink, may it please you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you'll get an answer Mr. Piletta-Zanin either later this day, or if you -- if an exchange of information, not necessarily in this courtroom, could help you out, that, of course, would be good as well. Then Mr. Usher, would you please, then, lead in Witness P.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome in this courtroom. I will call you "Mrs. P" because there are protective measures in effect. That means that we'll not mention your name, and that your face is distorted on our screens. Before you testify in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of the solemn declaration is handed out to you now by the usher. And may I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. You will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution, then you'll be examined by counsel for the Defence, and if there are any questions of the Judges, they will put them to you as well. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to hand to you a document. And I wish you to remember to answer my questions precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, could the witness be handed Document P3669.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Please, Mr. Usher, would you give this document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the time being, do not answer me; just have a quick look at that document. And please now answers my questions yes or no. Do you see your name on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you see your date of birth on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It could be now retrieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us -- may I just ask, do you live in Sarajevo, madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And for about how long have you lived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: 53 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I take it that you lived there during the conflict in the early 1990s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: During this conflict, can you just tell us the part of Sarajevo that you lived in? Don't tell us your address, just the district of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Logavina, Vrbanjusa, Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember sometime around the 10th of November, 1995, being interviewed by an investigator of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you mark for him a map of Sarajevo with the approximate location of where you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if I showed you that map again, would you be able to identify it again with your mark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, Your Honours, could the witness be shown Document P3670.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Usher, would you assist in giving the map to the witness. Don't put it on the ELMO yet. Is it -- I see that the yellow sticker is on it. I just wanted to be sure. So you may put it on the ELMO again, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Have a look at the document. You could look at the document to your right. Now, is that the map which you marked for our investigator? Just answer this before we get to the map. Is that the map that you marked for the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look, please, and tell us if you see a red X on it. Witness P, the map is to your right. You could look at the map itself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You point to a red X on the map. Is that the approximate location of the place you lived in in the early 1990s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I have lived there since 1960.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, the house in which you live, how many floors is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: There's the ground floor and two more floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which floor do you live on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: On the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, do you have a front window at that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, in the course of the conflict in the early 1990s, did you observe anything in respect of shelling and sniping in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would like you to focus on the period from September 1992 to August 1994. What can you tell the Court in respect to shelling in Sarajevo in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: During the war, I was in Sarajevo. I worked throughout the war. I would have to pass through the town. Everything was shelled. And from the window of my house, I was able to see the firing positions. When you're looking straight ahead from my window, the view is not obstructed in any way, so it was possible for me to see the positions from which the shelling came.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: From --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which district could you see from which the shelling came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Borije, straight ahead. Then to the right, Trebevic. And Spicasta Stijena on the left-hand side, with Mrkovici just above it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's start with Borije. You said Borije in front. By that I take it you mean that if you stood at your front window looking out, Borije was straight ahead of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, when you said that you could see the positions from which the shelling came, what do you mean by positions? I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't think that the witness stated that the Borije neighbourhood was straight ahead of her, opposite from her window. Could Mr. Stamp tell us exactly where in the testimony of the witness we can find that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what I see at this moment on my screen, on page 6, line 18, the question was, "Which district could you see from which the shelling came?" And the answer was: "Borije, straight ahead."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right, Mr. President. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are accepted, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you said you can see the positions from which the shelling came, what do you mean by "positions"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I was able to see the area of Borije because I'm facing the area of Borije from my window. So I was able to hear the sound and to see the smoke which resulted from the firing when it comes to the shelling which occurred during the day. Likewise, I could see the same from Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And Trebevic is which direction from your house, if you are at your front window facing straight out? Is it to your right, left, or in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: On my -- there's Borije right ahead of me, and Trebevic on the right-hand side, Spicasta Stijena on the left-hand side, with the area of Mrkovici above Spicasta Stijena, but I could not see Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, when you say that you could see the positions from where the shelling came from Trebevic, what do you mean by "positions"? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I was able to see a tank, or rather tanks, which were dug in and from where you first hear a sound, and then you see the smoke, and you know what's going on. I could never see a shell being fired during the day. I could see the actual shell only during the night because it is a ball of fire, so you can see it only during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the fire that you observed from Borije and Trebevic, can you say which part of the city was shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes. The old town, or Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said -- let me just ask you this: The areas of Borije and Trebevic from which you saw the shelling were in control of what party to the conflict? Do you know? Was it the Bosnian Serb army or the army of the federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Of the Serbian Montenegrin army with Karadzic's volunteers and supporters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, you said there was shelling from the area of Mrkovici but you could not see Mrkovici. How did you know that there was shelling of the city from Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Every shell that was fired passed over my house, above my house, because my house is the tallest one in the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And how would you know that a shell passed over your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: This time, it was flying very low, very low over the house. And actually, it fell very close to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How would you know if it is flying low over your house? Did you observe anything --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I could tell by the sound. No, no, but it was by the sound that I could tell that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What sound was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: It was a piercing sound. I was -- I happened to be at the window when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I turn you to the 5th of February, 1994. I'd like to direct you to that date. That day, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: At the window of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Were you alone at home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No. I was with my son, who was 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many children do you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who -- without calling a name, what did your other child do during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: My other son was in the army. But he had broken his arm because a log had fallen on his arm and so, for about a year, he was not at the front line, in the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thanks. So he was in the army. Can you please remember to answer my questions briefly. We are trying to move as quickly as possible. At about 12.00 that day, where in particular were you in your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I said -- sorry, I was at home, at the window, talking with a neighbour living above me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While you were there talking with your neighbour, did anything happen that you noticed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: It was incredibly quiet, a very calm day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you notice anything while you were there talking with your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No. No. Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Can you say what the weather was like that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Quite nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And while you were there at your window talking with your neighbour, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: We heard a bang -- I mean, that something was fired. And there was this strident sound going over the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The sound you heard, the bang you heard, from which direction did it come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: From Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About what time did you hear this bang?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: It was 12.00, 20 past 12.00, thereabouts. I'm not quite sure. I don't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, after you heard that bang, did you hear or observe anything in the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: And then we heard a harsh sound, and I knew that that shell had fallen nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you said you heard a "harsh sound," could you describe it just a little bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Whistles]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I describe that sound as something like a whistle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Whistles]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, she whistled and then she said "boom."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you hear any sound like that in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, no. It was a single shell, the only shell that was fired that day in the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, from your window to the place you call Spicasta Stijena, is there any impediment to your line of sight? In other words, is there anything between where you were at your window and Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In other words, you can stay at your window and see --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Spicasta Stijena is a sheer drop. It is just a rock, and there's a sheer drop.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. For the time being, I'm just interested to know if you can see Spicasta Stijena from your window.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know what happened in the town after you heard the sound of the thing being fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: People who were nearby were running towards the street, towards buildings, and shouting, "Markale, Markale."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, you said that you observed or knew of shellings in the city. In your own particular neighbourhood, do you know of any shelling in particular? Or may I just quickly, for the sake of -- direct your mind to the 12th of June, 1993. Did anything in particular happen on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: There was a funeral taking place at the cemetery, and a shell was fired which killed ten of those present.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Above my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was the cemetery in the territory of the federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And was this place above your house in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said ten people died. Do you know if they were civilian or military people who died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: It was a funeral, mother of one of those killed was being buried. Two of her sons were killed, and eight more persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question I asked, if you knew whether or not those persons killed or injured were civilians or military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In your district, in the district that you live at, what time of the day did funerals normally take place at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: At noon, and at times, even at night. Because my neighbourhood Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was under very intensive shellfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that why funerals sometimes took place at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness P. I have nothing further in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, everybody. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness P.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Today you confirmed to us that on the 19th of November, 1995, you gave a statement to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us that with the investigators of the OTP, you talked also on the 24th of June, 2001, and the 16th of September, 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: To be quite honest, I don't remember the days but I did talk with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you talked with them on two more occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: They came to Sarajevo, and I went to talk with them, that is, make my statements, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How many statements did you make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I gave two statements, a statement which has to do with our Ministry of the Interior of the federation of B and H. That was the first statement that I gave.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us in what part of Sarajevo you lived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: That is where I still live.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And on the map, you marked the location of the part of the city where you lived and still live, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence should like to show the witness the map, this map, because the Defence wishes to ask the witness certain questions relative to the allegations made by the witness during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The map is being prepared, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Usher, would you please put the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us today that you had seen shelling and sniping in the course of the conflict in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on this map the location of Borije.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Will you pick up the black marker and next to the place where you put the red cross, mark the direction leading towards Borije.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes, Mr. Usher, we always use blue for markings on request of the Prosecution, and black for markings on the request of the Defence. Could you please, Mr. Usher, move the map in such a way or have it zoomed out that we can see what the witness is doing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, from the location which you marked with a red cross, will you draw a line to show the direction of Borije.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: May I draw it across the map?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can do on the map. And will you make it an arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has drawn a straight line and an arrow facing westward marking the direction of Borije.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you mind making it the east instead of the west. Yes, please. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Thank you, Your Honour. The witness has drawn an eastward arrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please, above this arrow, will you put letter B to mark the direction of Borije.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us today that from this direction, you watched the city being shelled.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, between April 1992 to August 1994, how often did you see shelling coming -- shelling of the city coming from this direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: All I can say is that every building in the area where I live, and you can see it on the map, was shelled. How many shells were fired, that is something I do not know, if you mean how many pieces.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Please, from April 1992 to end of 1992, how often was the part of the city in which you say almost every house was shelled, how often were they shelled from that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: The shelling never ceased.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "never ceased," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I mean very often by day and by night. That was the worst period insofar as the shelling of Stari Grad was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which was that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: 1992, beginning to the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: 1993, what was shelled in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: The whole area was shelled, but all that time, in 1992 until the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you now about 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, you asked me about 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And you've answered it, and now I'm asking you about 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I see. I'm sorry. There was less shelling then of my area, the area where I live.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: There was intermittent shelling, but not like in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since you have drawn an arrow in the direction of Borije, you told us that the army of Republika Srpska was at Borije. Can you confirm for us that in the area of Kovaci and Vratnik, towards Sedrenik, you know that part of the city, that the 9th Mountain Brigade was quartered there? That is, the 10th Mountain Brigade commanded by Topalovic was quartered there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I'm not a military expert, nor do I know that. That is to begin with. Secondly, I cannot see all of Vratnik to know where is who, because after all, at that time, I was working.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You've just told us that you were working.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you spent almost -- you spent at work most of your days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Well, at times 24 hours, but I had to cross all of Sarajevo to reach my workplace.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You confirmed to us that you could not see Vratnik particularly well from your part of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: What you are saying, what that is, I cannot see the cemetery of Kovaci. All I can see is a part line towards Borije, up there, because Borije is the area that I can see best, and it's a slope with low growth, with low vegetation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far is Borije from your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How many kilometres is Borije far?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: You mean as the crow flies or -- ?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Both as the crow flies and --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Well, it is -- it is near enough for me to see shots being fired by the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you worked 24 hours a day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, when did you watch shots being fired from Borije?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I could always watch it when I was at home. When I was at home, I could always see shots being fired from Trebevic and Borije because it is directly in my line, in my field of vision.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you watched shots fired from Borije, tell us, what did you see? What buildings were shelled at those times when you watched shots being fired from Borije?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I do not see where shells fall, because I told you, in daytime I could not see those shells. I could see them being fired, the moment of their being fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. P, may I ask you, once a question has been put to you by counsel for the Defence, just to make a brief pause because everything you say and what Ms. Pilipovic says has to be translated. Yes? Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that your son was in the -- had been in the army. Can you tell us, when did he join the army of BH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: My son left in -- in October 1991, my son was released from the military service of the former JNA. And in July 1992, he joined the army of BH.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which military formation was your son attached to? Was it a brigade, which brigade, or a smaller unit, and which brigade was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Believe me that I never discussed it with him, nor did he ever give me any information.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the BH army, was your son issued with a uniform and a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what did you know that he was a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Because he went, but he carried food for the mess.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And where was the mess and which unit it belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I don't know, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And where was the mess, in what part of the city? Where did he go to the positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I don't know where he went to when he went to positions. But the mess was in the old part of the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was it in the vicinity of the part of the city that you told us was called Logavina, and there is an elementary school there, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that in elementary school was the headquarters of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: All I can confirm is that I used to see uniformed soldiers. Whether it was the headquarters of that, I cannot say -- I mean, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But you are confirming for us that in that school you used to see uniformed soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, not in the school. Outside, in the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when talking with the OTP investigators on the 6th of September, 2000, you said that there was a local school in Logavina which the Bosnian Army had taken over. Is that correct? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, on the basis of what information did you confirm that the Bosnian Army had taken over the school at Logavina, on Logavina Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes, I can, because I have to pass by that school when I go to work, or shopping. Children did not attend that school, and I can say because I saw soldiers walk in to that school.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, can you tell us how far is that school from the part of the city that you had marked as your neighbourhood? How far from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: 500 metres below my -- the building that I live in.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us today about the shelling from Trebevic. Can you indicate on the map which part of Trebevic can you see from the part of the city in which you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate on the map the direction in which you see Vidikovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the record, the witness has drawn an eastward arrow to point at the direction of Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I only want you to put letter T in that corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may it be southeast.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I said that, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I think I heard "east," but we agree that it's southeast, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in that direction that you marked, will you please put T.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, letter T means direction Trebevic. At this part of the examination, will you please mark where that street is where the school was in which the BH army was quartered.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Well, move parallelly with my house, and you'll find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I merely want you to place a small black cross on the street where the school is, approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: This is my street, the length of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, just put a circle to show where the school is. Just a circle in which you will put number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Just a slightly larger circle in which you will write number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]. I put it outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness -- the witness made a large black dot with number 1 above it to mark the school on Logavina Street where the BH army was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you marked for us the southeast, and you told us that you could see Vidikovac. Could you now tell us which area of the town was shelled from that direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: The old part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, how many times did you see the old part of the town being shelled from that direction? How many times did you personally observe that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly how many times, but I know that it was on quite a few occasions, at least 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that it was on at least 50 occasions. Out of these 50 occasions, could you single maybe two or three shelling incidents of the old part of the town that you were able to observe, and can you tell us what is it that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Usually, the target was the houses. One of the impact points was the old brewery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark for us the location of the brewery in the area that you said you saw being shelled.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it with number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Witness has just made a circle. Underneath, she wrote number "2," having thus indicated the location of the brewery which the witness has told us was shelled from the direction of Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you now tell us approximately on what date this incident occurred? Tell us the year: 1992, 1993, or 1994.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: It was on the 15th of January, 1993, that 15 people were killed near the brewery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this personally, and do you know any of the people who were killed on the 15th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know the Lacovic [phoen] couple, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: By the surname of Lacovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes. Azra and Asim Lacovic were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, two of their children sustained very serious injuries also.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any knowledge as to the fact that there was the Bistrik barracks in the area of the town which was shelled on the 15th of January, 1993, and that that barracks was used by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the area that you said was shelled on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes. But there's also a Catholic church in that part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In this area where the BH army was, do you know that there was constant fighting near the Colina Kapa and Mala Kapa areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, the brewery belongs to the centre of the town. It is not situated on the slopes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When facing Vidikovac, and you said that you were able to see Vidikovac, from your house, when facing Vidikovac, is it possible to see the elevations which are called Mala Kapa and Colina Glava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that throughout the conflict, both Colina Glava and Mala Velika Kapa were under the BH army control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the shelling of the cemetery on the 12th of June, 1993, can you tell us whether this is something that you eyewitnessed or just heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I was at home when this crowd of people started rushing down the street from that location, those who were dispersed after the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you did not personally see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time come to know from which part of the town the funeral gathering was shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know that the shelling came from the direction where the VRS positions are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible, because you could see both Trebevic and Borije from that area, but I personally didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So once again, you're telling us that you don't know the direction from which the funeral column was shelled on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about the 5th of February in your testimony today, and you said that you happened to be at the window when you heard what exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: When I heard the shell being fired, that is, the sound which I could hear coming from above my house, and I could also feel the detonation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you told us that you heard the shell being fired. Can you describe for us the sound. What is it exactly that you heard? You said you heard the shell being fired, but what kind of sound is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Well, you usually hear a "boom" sound. I believe I've already mentioned this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that it was on the basis of this sound that you knew that the shell was fired from the positions in Mrkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: If it had come from Borije or Trebevic, I would have seen the smoke. But I'm sure that this was fired from Mrkovici because the shell had flown over my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Please finish.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: And it didn't go very far, and the detonation was very loud.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that Mrkovici is behind your house, and that you cannot see that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No. They are situated in a forest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is just a matter of the translation I got. I can't recall the witness saying that Mrkovici is or was behind her house, which is what my friend just put to the witness. If I'm -- I think my friend agrees that perhaps that was not entirely correct and will rephrase the question, I imagine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you approximate for us with respect to your house the direction of Mrkovici on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you mark the area with a letter M and place an arrow also.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness has drawn an arrow pointing northeast and marked with letter M the location of Mrkovici with respect to the area where she lives.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, how far is Mrkovici in relation to your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Before the war, I sometimes used to walk to Mrkovici. It would take me one hour to get there. I couldn't tell you exactly how many kilometres that is, but it is more or less one hour's walk.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the way to Mrkovici, you must have passed through Sedrenik and the seven wood area, Sedam Suma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes, let me just add that I can see the area of seven woods from my window.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that during the conflict, that is, in 1992, 1993, and 1994, in the area which you can see, the area of the seven woods, that the positions of the 105th Motorised Brigade of the BH army were, that that was where those positions were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in 1992, 1993, and 1994, there was fighting going on in that part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to the direction where the area of the seven woods lie, is that the area where Spicasta Stijena and Grdo Brdo are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes, it is in the same direction more or less, but it's difficult for me to say. It is in the direction of Grdonja. Grdonja and Spicasta Stijena are to the left of the seven woods' area when I'm looking from my window.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on the map, would you please indicate for us the area of Grdonja, Spicasta Stijena, and Sedam Suma, that is the seven woods' area, and mark them for us on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please take care that the marking is done as much as possible on the ELMO so that we can see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You have drawn two lines. Could you mark one of them with number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness has marked with a horizontal line the area of Sedam Suma, and marked it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now mark with number 2 the area above the first line, and can you confirm for us that you have thus marked the area of Grdonja.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark for us the location of Spicasta Stijena as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please mark with number 3 the area where you say can see Spicasta Stijena, and would you please encircle this number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness has made a circle in which she has written number 3. According to her testimony, it indicates the area of the seven woods where Spicasta Stijena is located.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that Spicasta Stijena rises above an abyss.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: What I mean to say is that you cannot climb up the Spicasta Stijena point from the ground below; that is, you cannot go up from the bottom to the top of the Spicasta Stijena point. The only way you can access the location is through Mrkovici and the villages above. That is the only way to go to Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever go to the bottom of Spicasta Stijena point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if there are any houses at the bottom of Spicasta Stijena point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far are they from the feature itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: They are just below the feature, that is, right underneath Spicasta Stijena point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When going towards Spicasta Stijena, what is the best position to see these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you take the route going to Grdonja, when you walk towards Spicasta Stijena point, can you see these houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are they also visible from the direction of the Spicasta Stijena point itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned the incident which took place on the 5th of February. You told us that the weather was quite fine. Can you be more specific, what kind of weather was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: It was so nice that it was -- that I was able to open the window. It was not that cold. It was not raining or snowing. The weather was mild.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was it sunny or overcast?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: There were sunny spells.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, when you were at the window when you said you heard the firing sound, how much time -- how much later did you hear the actual explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Well, I'm not an expert to be able to see that. I mean, I would have to go to the shooting range and see how -- what happens when a shell is fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you actually see anything, apart from hearing the sound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that your son was a member of the army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was he supposed to go back to the front line on the 5th of February?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: As I told you, my son was on sick leave, which lasted for about a year. He had had an arm fracture.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But you told the investigator that your son was supposed to go back to the front line on the 5th of February?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes, he was supposed to go back, but since he had had this fracture, since he had broken his arm, he didn't go.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When he was on the front line, how long was his shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where did he take his meals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: At the canteen, but he would carry his own meals.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you're telling us that your son worked at the canteen which prepared food for the troops. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the part of the town with respect to your neighbourhood where this military canteen was, and can you mark it for us on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, I cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know on which street it was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you worked throughout that period of time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where was your work? Where did you go to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: In Novo Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In what particular street, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: In Vojvode Putnika Street, as it was called then.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say Novo Sarajevo, are you referring to the area of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Cengic Vila.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the area, in the neighbourhood where you worked, were there any troops, and where were they located? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was the Vranica company located in that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I don't know. The street I took was called Putim Zivota. It was impossible for us to walk by the Marsal Tito barracks because of sniping. For the first two or three months, it was impossible for me to go to work.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that there was sniping coming from Marsal Tito barracks during the first two months. What particular months do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: May and June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about any fighting going on between members of the JNA who were located in the Marsal Tito barracks and who were being attacked by the green berets, and the members of the Territorial Defence, that is, the BH army, in the months of May and June 1992 in the vicinity of Marsal Tito barracks? Do you know that that barracks was attacked and shot at? Did you know that from the media?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Well, very often there were power cuts. I didn't see any such programme on TV. But I know that it was impossible to walk in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What is it that you heard exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Well, I heard from other people that there was sniping going on in that area, and I couldn't go to work.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the fire was opened from the Energoinvest and Unis buildings on this barracks, that the barracks were shot at from the surrounding buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, I told you that for about two months I didn't go to that neighbourhood. It was impossible because of the sniping.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that you personally did not see that, that this is just something that you heard from others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you said you heard about that, are you referring to the media or rumours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Well, I am referring to what other people talked about. We didn't have any electricity or water. Well, the electricity would come from time to time but we didn't have water at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you're telling us that from time to time, there were power and water cuts. In 1993 and 1992, how often were you without electricity and water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Well, it would be much easier for me to tell you how often we had electricity and water, and not the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I think that throughout the war, we had electricity for about 20 days maximum, and we didn't have water at all, at no time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the water tank that you went to, that is, what was the water tank for your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, we did not have any water tank. We didn't have any water. However, when there was water, we had to go to the Felacici tank, water tank.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know under whose control that part of the town was where the water supply was for your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: It was under the BH army, while there was water.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you be more specific? You said while there was water, it was under the BH army control. What exactly do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: The water tank was under the BH army control. As for the other side of the town where some of my family members lived and where some of my friends lived, they had the Jahorina source, but it was closed during the war because the area was, as I have already indicated, under the control of --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Under the control of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what is the name of that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Bistrik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the Prosecution took 28 minutes for examination-in-chief. You took 45 minutes by now for cross-examination. I didn't want to stop you at an early stage, but would you please keep that in mind. And also perhaps keep in mind that we usually have a break at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you confirmed to us that the area of the town in question was Trebevic under the VRS control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As for the area which was under the BH army control, they did have some water supplies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: Yes. But the area which was under the VRS control, they did not allow any water, and I am sure about that. I claim this with full responsibility, because the brewery incident wouldn't have happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You're telling us that you claim this with full responsibility. Is this something that you knew personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: I told you that my relatives and my friends lived there, so I knew personally about that. I would take water from Logavina to Bistrik.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there were repairs being made in respect of electricity and water in this part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No, no, because when there's shelling, no repairs are possible irrespective of the side involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the UN observers were there in that part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this concludes our examination of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No re-examination. Mrs. P, you've answered all the questions put to you by the Prosecution and the Defence. The Judges have no further questions. This means that this concludes your examination. I know that you had to wait Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. for quite some time before you could come to this courtroom. We feel sorry for that. We also know that it's quite something to come from a far distance and to testify in this Court. We do hope that you understand that it's important for this Court to hear from those who have been present during the relevant times and the relevant places of what happened, so we are very glad that you came to answer the questions of the parties. And after having thanked you for coming, I wish you a safe trip home again. Mr. Usher, would you be lead Mrs. P out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, I think two documents were tendered in evidence: The first one the name sheet, P3669, the second one, a marked map, P3670. I think that's all. Yes, P3670 was premarked in red, but has been marked during the examination of the witness with black markings on it. Since both documents contain the name of the witness, they are both admitted under seal. It's 11.00 now. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I see you're on your feet. You'd like to repeat the question to Mr. Ierace now or -- ?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, just to indicate that there will be no objections to the exhibits, but we would appreciate if the following maps could also have the elevations indicated so that we know at what altitude the dwellings are located, which is something that we don't know on these maps. But it is very useful, and we will be able to read this, hopefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, these maps that are premarked by the witness during the statements, of course, we can't put in any elevation lines on from that moment. But as we -- as I asked before, that this Court would be quite happy if the parties could provide the Court with a map. I don't know. You told us that you're discussing the matter with the Prosecution. I don't know whether there are any elevation lines in it. But if you think it's important, perhaps your choice might be that it's one which also shows the elevation. May I just draw the attention of Mr. Ierace to the fact that Mr. Piletta-Zanin did put a question to the Prosecution this morning in the beginning. I don't know whether you'd like to give an answer right away or do it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I heard the comments by Mr. Piletta-Zanin. The answer is a short one. The documents to which I referred last Thursday were indexed and that index was provided to the Defence in mid last year. And as I understand it, the index indicated the source of each document. Those sources were variously brigades, battalions of the 1st Corps, the command of the 1st Corps, and I think there were -- there was at least one document which issued from the main staff of the ABiH. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's three minutes past 11.00. After the break, Mr. Ierace, Mr. Stamp, I think we'll proceed with the videolink testimony of the next witnesses. So we'll -- everything is prepared for that, I assume. Yes, I see Madam Registrar nodding that everything is prepared. So we'll then have a break until 11.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that all the problems with the videolink have been solved. I was also told that the problem was caused because the Prosecution did not inform the technicians what kind of technical facilities they would need. It's a pity for this half an hour, but let's just proceed. At this very moment, I see a picture on my screen of Sarajevo, and I see a representative of the Registry. Could we just check, Ms. Philpott, whether the connection is working well. Could you please speak a few more words so that we can see. I just heard part of one word.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The sound quality is still rather poor. Could you perhaps, Madam Registrar, just speak two or three lines.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count one, two, three, four, five, six, seven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I counted with you until seven. Let's just see whether it's -- the quality is good enough to start. If not, we'll have to interrupt. And I'm not aware of whether this is the usual quality or whether we usually have a better quality. Then, Mr. Ierace, I have a list in front of me of the 13th of March indicating what the order of appearance will be for the videolink witnesses. Is that still the valid one?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, please, Mr. Ierace, could you call your first witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the first witness I've called via videolink is Nura Bajraktarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are orders for facial distortion and voice distortion for this witness that were made last Friday, I think, by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because they are not on the list of the 13th of March, but they are effective.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I note that the face distortion is not working on the screen. Perhaps we should go into closed session until we have sorted this out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps -- could we just check with the technicians whether ... Ms. Philpott, we have a technical problem as far as the face distortion is concerned. We would rather first sort this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There is not an order for voice distortion. I correct myself on that point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It just has been confirmed to me that the facial distortion is effective for all those images that are broadcasted out of our own system, but we can see the witness with normal images on our screens. Mrs. Bajraktarevic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give testimony for this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you now. May I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid that the sound quality is not good enough for the interpreters to make any translation. We have -- Ms. Philpott, we have a bad sound quality so that the interpreters are not able to translate what the witness says. Perhaps you'd invite her to sit down for a while so that she doesn't have to stand while we are solving our technical problems. May I ask the technicians whether the sound quality will improve.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we try one more time ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Philpott, could you please ask the witness to sit down and come closer to the microphone and see whether this will be of any help.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I just check now with the interpreters whether the quality of the sound is sufficient to translate whatever is said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Your Honour, we haven't heard enough in order to be able to tell you whether it's going to be feasible or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shall we perhaps first start. Whenever you feel that you're not able to do the translation, then you immediately --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We will let you know, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mrs. Bajraktarevic. Before your testimony will start, I first have to see what Mr. Piletta-Zanin, Defence counsel, will tell us. Please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I don't know what kind of sound the interpreters are able to hear. The Defence likes to hear the floor, hear everything that is being said. But my colleague is telling me that she cannot hear enough in order to understand, and I'm in more or less the same situation. If the quality doesn't improve, I think that we will have to give up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll see what to do if the quality will not improve. Let's just first start, and let's give it a try for a couple of minutes, and then I'll hear from both the interpreters and from the Defence whether we could proceed or not. Ms. Bajraktarevic, you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is your name Nura Bajraktarevic?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you 71 years of age?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 28th of February, 1931.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you lived in the Soukbunar area of Sarajevo all your life?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. That's where I was born also.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is Soukbunar south of the city of Sarajevo, of Skenderija?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During the war between 1992 and 1995, did you have to collect wood for cooking?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you sometimes collect wood from an area called Brajkovac?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand your question. I couldn't hear you very well. Yes, I have now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Did you sometimes collect wood from an area called Brajkovac?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is Brajkovac a few kilometres further away from the city from where you live?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you collected wood during the war, did you sometimes see people you knew also collecting wood?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you collected wood in Brajkovac, did you ever hear shooting?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On one occasion, when you were collecting wood, was someone near you shot?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On one occasion when you were in the Brajkovac area, was there someone you knew who was in the same area and who was shot?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question. The witness has just answered "no" in response to a question which was practically the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps, Mr. Ierace, I think the objection is justified. You asked a question which had been answered. At the same time, I can imagine that sometimes, for whatever reason, that you're so surprised by an answer on the basis of the investigations that you would seek the assistance of the Chamber in order to verify whether there's any misunderstanding. But just repeating the question in order to get another answer might not be the way of doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there was a difference in the questions asked. There was a critical difference, and I think that accounts for the different answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just then check again. You mean to say that it might have happened when she was not collecting wood. That's the difference I see in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the precise moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't notice that difference. Perhaps I should have seen it. But whenever -- the question was almost the same but not entirely the same. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I should have perhaps read first again the questions and see what the difference was. There was a difference, so when I said that the objection was justified, I'm afraid I made a mistake. I apologise for that. And Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, who was the person you knew who was shot?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Sacir. The surname escapes me at the moment. I forgot his surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: During the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember what year?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember what season it was when he was shot?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: It was summertime.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you see him when he was shot?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't see him. I couldn't see him because he was higher up the hill, and I didn't dare get up. I was trying to hide myself. I was squatting, and this other friend who was with us, he saw when he was shot. And he said, "Oh, dear." And I said "what happened?" And he said, "Sacir just got killed."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the name of the other friend?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Bajrami.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that you were crouching at the time. How many shots did you hear?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: That time, I heard only one shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How long was it before you heard that shot that you had last seen Sacir?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Immediately. And this friend of mine told me to get him some water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you do when Bajrami told you to get him some water?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I went to a neighbouring house and asked for water, and the woman there gave me some water. And Bajrami told me to bring it up there. But I said I couldn't. I'm afraid I would also be hit by a bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you do with the water that the woman gave you?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I put it on a wall and left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately what time of day was it when Sacir was shot?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: It was around mid-day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you arrive in that area that morning?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would usually get there by 9.00 or 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately what time that morning did you first see Sacir?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: That morning, I didn't see him when he came. I only saw him when he was already chopping wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you gone there that day to collect wood?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: That day, I was gathering wood, yes. And when he was shot, I left home. I just didn't dare continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean you left to go home?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately --

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: And I went to see Sacir's wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to object at this point. A moment ago, you overruled my objection because apparently there was a difference between the first question asked by Mr. Ierace, that is, "Did you sometimes chop wood in this area?" That is the question contained this element, and the second question, "when you were at Brajkovac." So we are now going back to this indirect question which can lead us to the same situation in which we were before I raised my objection. This way, we are now, it seems to me, going back to square one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'll have a look at the questions. I would say that your objection was that a question was put again which had been answered before. The first question was, "When you collected wood in Brajkovac, did you ever hear shooting?" And then, "On one occasion when you were collecting wood, was someone near you shot?" The answer was "No." And the next question was: "On one occasion when you were in Brajkovac area, was there someone you knew who was in the same area and who was shot?" The answer was "Yes." The difference between the two questions is that in the first question, there was specifically asked for a situation where the witness was collecting wood when noticing that someone was shot, while this specification was not in the second question. Now, the last question was whether the witness had gone there to collect wood. And the answer was a bit besides the question that she was gathering wood.
