So the questioning as such, I would say, is not the same. And at the same time, it might turn out a possibility which I had in mind Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as a matter of fact as a possible explanation for what happened, that there might have been some misunderstanding. I do not see any reason at this moment to stop Mr. Ierace from his line of questioning. Please, Mr. Ierace, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, approximately how old was Sacir?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I said I couldn't tell you exactly. He may have been 60 or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What sort of clothes was he wearing that day that he was shot?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you see him that day carrying any firearms?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No. No, he wasn't carrying.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you see that morning in that area any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before that day, when you were in that area, had you been shot at?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On other occasions before that day when you went to that area to collect wood, had anyone fired a gun at you or in your direction?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: There was constant shooting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage, I would like the witness to view a video. Although the witness appears in the video and throughout it has her back to the camera, it may be prudent that it be shown in closed session because it has not -- the head area has not been pixilated, given the late stage of the application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any observation from the Defence to be made on the request to go in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I merely wish to inform the Chamber that we have just received the tape, the video, that my learned friends want us to view.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't want to do anything other than -- I don't want to do anything other than continue with this witness's testimony, but I note the tape was disclosed on the 26th of October last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What number is it, has it, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The number is V000-3484. It is Exhibit Number 3280S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit Number 3280S is on the list. I didn't hear prior to this hearing any complaint of the Defence that it would not have -- that this exhibit would not have been disclosed. Mrs. -- Madam Registrar, could we please go in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are now in open session again. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mrs. Bajraktarevic. At the time -- at the time that Sacir was shot, were you on the embankment above the road in the direction that you pointed?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, shortly, on the screen in front of you, you will see a photograph. Would you please tell us when you can see the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, I refer to the electronic 360-degree photograph which is P3279S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, do you have the photograph on the screen in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise what appears in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: It's not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We believe the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will move the photograph. Do you recognise the town or city which appears in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is that place?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can see from where the place fired from, that is Osmice, and that thing down there is the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I will move the photograph again. Mrs. Bajraktarevic, do you recognise the area where the camera is positioned? What part of Sarajevo is that?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise -- could you please repeat those last few words.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the place.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No, we cannot get the witness. There are too many interruptions. We are sorry. It was impossible to understand the witness's -- what the witness was saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the quality of the sound is so bad, the Defence cannot hear, and I see that the interpreters again cannot get it all. And I believe we have to know what the consequences will be. We have to draw them, and I say unfortunately, and three times unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Chamber experienced until now that the interpreters seemed to be able to translate usually what was said by the witness and indicate immediately if they are not able to translate. When it will not be significantly more, I invite those examining the witness to ask for a repetition of the answer when the interpreters have indicated that they could not hear the witness. So Mr. Ierace, if you would please do that. And the Chamber is paying a lot of attention on the question of whether at a certain moment the general level of understanding would fall below an acceptable standard. Could you please, Mr. Ierace, perhaps repeat the question, or at least invite the witness to repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, I asked you if you recognised the area where the camera was positioned and what part of Sarajevo it was. At first you said, "No"; then you said, "Yes, I recognised the place." And then you said something after that which we did not hear. Could you please repeat what you said after the words: "Yes, I recognise the place."

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I recognise the place, but this is -- this is Mahala Brajkovac. That is what I think, because I don't often go up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, may I ask you to pause once the question has been put to you, that you take just a brief pause before answering the question. That's for technical reasons. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, I have moved the photograph again, and now you should be able to see a tree on the right which extends from the bottom of the screen to the top of the screen. And in the bottom right hand half of the picture, there is a flat green area which has a silver car in front of it. Do you recognise that flat green area? Do you know what it is?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I think that it could be the reservoir, or I said I didn't often go up there. Perhaps somebody is building something here. I mean, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you anywhere near the reservoir when you heard the shot that you understand killed Sacir?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We think the witness said.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: That's right, to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, could you please repeat that last answer. We did not hear all of the words perhaps.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I said Sacir was killed on the left-hand side, and what you see down there, I think it is the reservoir, or perhaps somebody's building something. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the video, we saw you standing on a road. Whereabouts was the reservoir in relation to that part of that road?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Below the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the hills which are behind the construction that you said may be the reservoir?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. Please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are losing the witness again.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't go there of late, you know, and I couldn't tell you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And we could not hear again the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, I'm sorry, but we did not hear everything you just said. Could you repeat your answer, speaking slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I said the reservoir was beneath the road which is slightly up there where I was, below the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recognise the hills which are dark on the photograph and are behind the construction that you said might be the reservoir?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: We called it Osmice and Baba -- one was called Baba something. I don't exactly those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time that Sacir was shot, which forces controlled Osmice and Baba? Were they the Serb forces or the Bosnian government forces, or some other forces?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Serb forces. Yes, that area up there, it was the Serb forces who was there. And down where we were, there were no troops at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which forces control --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm really very sorry, but two things: I do not know where Baba something, I do not know what that refers to, but this is something that I see in this text. Now I'm trying to follow on the Serb channel to see how we can hear the witness, and please believe me that this is an exercise which is not only difficult, which at times becomes impossible. And I think that General Galic behind me thinks the same thing. It is simply impossible to understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as a matter of fact, I changed - although I do not understand the language - a couple of times to the B/C/S channel as well in order to get an impression. And I imagine that perhaps my colleagues did as well, so let me just confer with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, of course we noticed that, at occasions, it was difficult to understand the witness. This Chamber at this moment relies on the interpreters. They indicated a few times that they could not understand what was said and therefore were not able to interpret. This Chamber takes it that if the interpreters are able to translate, and it's not just one interpreter but several of them who have to interpret, if they can understand it, even if it's difficult, and since this Chamber trusts that whenever they feel that they could not or were hesitant to do so, they will indicate this, the Chamber thinks that we could proceed. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, what was Baba?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: It was in front of so-called Osmice, where those Serb forces were, so-called Osmice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What does Baba look like?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a boulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you see it in the photograph which is in front of you now? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I think that it's to the right above those buildings, as far as I can see. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "above those buildings," what colour are the buildings in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: White.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will move the photograph slowly to the right. If it is the wrong direction, please tell me. Is that the direction that you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think this is just too leading for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer given by the witness was not very clear. So, Mr. Ierace, you should be in a position to ask for a clarification of the answer. Whether the way he did it was so clear for the witness that we could expect a more precise answer, that's a different matter. I had some difficulties in understanding the question, Mr. Ierace. So perhaps if you could rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, you said that you think that Baba was to the right above the white buildings. Can you see Baba in the photograph now?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. I saw it before. But if you took me there, I'd give you all the places. But like this -- and I cannot quite follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the video you were asked to point in the direction that you heard the shot. What was in that direction? What places?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Osmice, so-called Osmice. I pointed at it, and there was another direction called Kula. Now where the bullet exactly came from, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which forces controlled Kula at that time?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Serb again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what area was Kula?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't get you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll withdraw that question. How far away was Kula from where you were when you heard the shot?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to tell you how many kilometres, but it's not all that far.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, perhaps we first explain to Sarajevo that we'll have a break. Mrs. Bajraktarevic, we will have a break now for one hour and a half. This means that your examination has not been concluded yet, but we'll continue after the lunch break, one hour and a half from now. Did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll adjourn until local time 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The technicians have tried to work hard to improve the quality of the sound. I hope it is better, and may I ask the Defence whenever there is a line or a word you cannot hear, of course you're always allowed to ask these lines or words to be repeated because bad sound quality shouldn't mean that you finally have no access to the testimony itself. Mr. Ierace, are you ready to resume your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, you will now see another photograph on the screen in front of you. Can you see the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You will notice that this photograph is taken from a road. In the background, having regard to your earlier evidence, do you recognise Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: It's not very visible.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, we do not have that picture on the screen here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's exactly the issue that I wanted to raise, that is the question that I wanted to ask. But I just heard Ms. Kelly saying that there's no photograph on the screen. Do we have it then, or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have it on our screen under the bottom, "computer evidence."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We have it now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I hear that Ms. Philpott confirms that they have it on the screen as well. If everyone has it on the screen, then please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, the screen is now displaying Exhibit P3279SS.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, do you recognise Sarajevo in the background of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I can see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will now move the photograph around to the right. Please accept from me that this photograph was taken on the spot where you were standing during the video that you saw this morning. I will continue to move the photograph to the right. On the video, you were seen to indicate the house which now appears on the screen as the place where you obtained some water or went for help. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said this morning that the reservoir was below this road, that is, I take it, the road which appears in the photograph. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but above the fence, towards the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: And then below the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I will continue to move the photograph to the right. We have now completed a complete circuit of the photograph. Mrs. Bajraktarevic, during the war, did you see anyone else who had apparently been shot in that area?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I stated that there was another woman who was gathering wood in more or less the same way, so she hadn't finished yet. The fog dispersed in the meantime, and then she continued. And then a bullet hit her in the stomach. I had already left by that time, but I could see her being taken away in a wheelbarrow or in a cart. She was later taken to hospital where she died.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know her name?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Fadila Peljto, Dila. That's what people called her, Dila.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Coming back to the photograph on the screen, do you happen to know the name of the road which appears in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: We called it Prasine. The road leading to Brajkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that completes examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Ms. Pilipovic, you're going to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, you'll now be examined by counsel for the Defence. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Bajraktarevic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that on the 6th of May, 2001, you gave a statement to the investigators of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I did give a statement, but I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to that interview which you gave to the investigators, did you have any other conversations of the kind, or was it the only one?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how it came about that you gave a statement to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: You know, there was this man who had probably been there to see them before, this friend of mine who saw the other man being hit. He was the one who gave the statement first. Since it was his friend who got killed, I think that it must have been his wife who told them my name, and that is how they came to know about me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I specifically ask your attention for a short pause between the next question. And, Mrs. Bajraktarevic, I see that you're answering the question already when you heard the first part of it. Would you please wait until the whole question has been put to you, and then perhaps wait for another second before answering the question because everything has to be translated, and if you speak the same language, it goes too quick for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Bajraktarevic, the person who gave the statement you said was the wife of the man, that is, that was the wife who referred the investigators to you, was that Sopi Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, who else could it have been?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. According to the translation of the witness's answer, she quite clearly said it was the man who gave the statement, not the man's wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I can see, that is -- Ms. Pilipovic, is there --?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't say that it was the wife of the late Sopi Bajrami who gave the statement. My colleague must have misunderstood me or maybe my words have been misinterpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think there might be some misunderstanding at this very moment. Please proceed. Could you perhaps rephrase the question in such a way --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that whatever misunderstandings there are, they will be taken away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Bajraktarevic, are you telling us that the gentleman whom you said is the late Bajram Sopi, was he the person who gave the statement to the investigators of the OTP and that it was the wife?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: That is what they told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Bajraktarevic, if I tell you that Mr. Sopi Bajram, in the statement that he gave to the investigators on the 27th of February, 1996, on page 2, case number 0090-6747, never at any point in time mentioned the fact that you were with him, can you tell us why it was that the late Sopi Bajram failed to mention you?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I can explain that: He didn't know me. As for Sacir, who was killed, it was his wife who knew me. She was the one who knew me. So I guess it must have been Sacir's wife who told them about me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know the late Sopi Bajram? Did you ever see him?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I used to see him very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where it was that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: He would pass by my house where I live. But I didn't have any contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the late Sacir Bosnic lived?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: The name of the street is, I think, Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before Sacir Bosnic was killed, did you associate with the Sacir -- that is, Bosnic family, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no. We would just greet each other when we saw each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How frequently did you go to that area of the town to gather wood?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes every day, and sometimes every few days.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that on that occasion when you went there to gather wood and when Sacir Bosnic was killed, had you already done so? Had you already been to that area to gather wood, or was that the first time?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I had already done so on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, when you came to the area to gather wood, did you ever hear about any shooting incidents in that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that there was a front line in that area of the town and that it was some 300 or 40 metres [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I guess that was the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which army was deployed in that part of the town; the BH army or the VRS?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know. It was the army of Republika Srpska that was deployed there, that is, up there in the higher ground, whereas there were no troops whatsoever in the area where we went to gather wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, with respect to the part of the town where you gathered wood, where the BH army positions were?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Below, below their positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the part of the city which you tell us is called Brajkovac, in relation to that part, because you say that the troops of the army of BH was below, can you tell us approximately where was the -- where were the troops of the army of BH, or Bosnian Army?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't say. I never went up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From that part of the city where you collected firewood, does one see hills called Colina Kapa, Mala, and Velika?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it's further on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if in that part of the city that you lived in, if there was a school there?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far was the school from the place where you lived?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was quite near.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that Bosnian soldiers gathered in the school when going to the front line, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is where they had their kitchen, their mess.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where did the soldiers sleep, those who had their meals there?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You lived in your house alone, or did you have your family with you?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: My husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And your sons?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: They were not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was one of your sons wounded during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was any other of your sons a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where your sons who are members of the BH army, where did they go to the positions? Where was their front line?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that, but in Sarajevo, basically.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the conflict, did they come to your place?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your sons who are members of the BH army in 1992, 1993, and 1994 come to your place, to your house?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what army unit did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President. I object on the basis of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please respond to the objection, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these questions are relevant. Through these questions, the Defence wishes to check the credibility of the witness, especially bearing in mind the statement which the witness gave to the OTP investigators on the 6th of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I fail to see how the identification of the army units to which this witness's sons belonged is in any way relevant to the credibility of this witness as to what she saw happen a couple of kilometres from where she lived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please respond, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when appreciating the statement of the witness during the examination-in-chief, the statement that she gave to the OTP investigators, bearing in mind that the witness does not remember either the time or the place or the time when the incident happened which she allegedly eyewitnessed, assessing her statement during the examination-in-chief, we believe it is relevant so as to check as credibility, to question the witness as regards where she lived, with whom she lived, and whether in the part of the city that she Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. lived in, there were any troops. During the examination-in-chief, the witness said that she never saw any soldiers or any military target; and yet today, when asked by the Defence, she said that near the place she lived, there was a school where soldiers gathered. The Defence only wishes to check whether in the school where the soldiers gathered there was any member of Witness Bajraktarevic's family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if that is what you seek to establish, whether any of the family members were there, you're entitled to do so. Please ask, then, that question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. -- Witness, did some member of your family, specifically your sons who were members of the BH army, did they come to the school?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you told us that that day, apart from that one shot, you did not hear anything else. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but let me tell you, I heard that shot. But there was fire which never stopped, but when Sacir was killed, I got frightened, and I went home because nobody dare go that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you answer truthfully how many shots did you hear at the moment when you were collecting wood with the late Bosnic?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No. Because I wasn't thinking about it. I wasn't giving it a thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that the late Bajrami Sopi who gave the statement to OTP investigators had said that there was gunfire before that, will you confirm that that was true?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: At that place, could you determine from which direction did this gunfire come?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, from which direction did the gunfire come?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I know that it came from two places. From which one of the two it came, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the first place that you identified as allegedly the source of fire, the Osmice motel?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Or perhaps Kula. I didn't really look at them. I didn't really look from where a bullet might come.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to what was in that area which you call Osmice? Were there any structures?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Earlier, there was a hotel; and below that, there was a locality.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there was a hotel, are you telling us that there is no more -- there are no hotels any more there?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I do not know. I did not go up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that this motel was destroyed and that in that motel, there was fighting between the two armies?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far is that area that you call Osmice, where the motel was, from the place where you collected firewood?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If you headed for that motel, how long would it take you to get to that place, walking?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I would take much, but I never checked.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if, in the area of the hotel that you say was called Osmice, there were any positions of the Bosnian Army?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if in that area, in that direction, towards Osmice hotel, there were any positions of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you tell us that the second place which you identify as a place from which gunfire could be opened was Kula --

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: -- can you then tell us, in relation to the place where you were collecting firewood, where was the place called Kula?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: From Osmice, and then further on, down.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "down," "further on," in which direction further on and down?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: To the right of Osmice. That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the area which leads to the road towards Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From your place where you say that you were at, collecting firewood, can you see that area that you say is called Kula? Can it be seen from there?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what do you claim that gunfire was opened from that position?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Why, one sensed that there was gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier on when you went there to collect firewood, did you also hear gunfire from that area that you say is called "Kula"?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I never thought about it. It was frequent.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us that that school which is near the place, that is, the house where you lived and soldiers went to that school, can you tell us, did you used to see those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, passing by.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what they wore?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, one knows how the army was dressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe -- can you describe it for us? Were they uniforms and what colour were they?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Camouflage, many-coloured.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the olive-green colour?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Why, yes, and yellow, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, can you tell us if those soldiers carried weapons?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where were the positions of those soldiers who came for their meals to that school?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. As a woman, it was not my business to inquire about them and look for their whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us the street on which that school was?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: It was called Kasindolska, and adjacent to Cicin Han.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that you, too, [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [redacted] I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to the reasons for the protective measures, I respectfully submit it is inappropriate for the witness to identify the place of her residence. And in my submission, the question, in any event, lacks relevance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, keeping in mind the protective measures, would you please respond.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- Your Honour, the witness did not say the number of the house or flat that he or she lived in, she only mentioned the street, and we think that revealing the identity of the street on which the witness lived will not cause unforeseen problems for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Hopefully my friend hasn't gone beyond the transcript. So I re-emphasise the need for my friend to respect the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll bear it in mind. I apologise. Perhaps it was a slight faux pas on the part of the Defence, but it wasn't deliberate in any way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that when the late Bajrami, who was at the same place where you were collecting wood, and that when -- that he asked you to bring water, is that true?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, who was in that house where you went to get the water?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So who was there?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: There was a woman who lived all by herself there. But I'd rather not mention her last name. And she has died meanwhile. She's dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you ask some other people to come and extend help to the late Sacir?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, who were those people?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I do not know who they were, but they were there nearby, and I begged them to help him. And they came, but I did not see them when they came because I had left straight away. I had gone home, and I went to see Sacir's wife to let her know that Sacir had been wounded so that she would go to the hospital if he would need blood or something so that he could be helped. But it was too late for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you just give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I seek that the transcript be redacted so as to preserve the effect of the protective measures. In particular, lines -- page 72, lines 1 and 2, and then the words spoken by my learned colleague at lines 11 through to 15 would overcome that problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I just ask you, if at page 71, line 25, last part would be redacted, and then, just for sake of certainty, page 72 line 1 because we do not know exactly what was said in the original language, and therefore I suggested that we would have not only line 1, but also line 2 up until "President." So if "Mr." is out, then I expect what the witness has said is also out, and perhaps the word "President" as well. Would that not solve the problem as far as lines 11 until 15 is concerned? Because reference is made to streets, but there is no street any more visible in the transcript before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have no objection to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Let me just confer with the registrar for one more second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you had talked with people who were near the place where you had been collecting firewood, and that you asked them to extend help to the late Bosnic. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We've lost the sound completely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have lost the sound. I cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, now we can hear you, Mrs. -- Witness. Can you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I did not know those people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if they lived there or if they were doing something there?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that in your statement that you gave to the OTP investigators on the 6th of May, 2001, on page 2 - number of the document is 0302-7350 - that you said, and I will quote the penultimate line: "Further on, in a house, there were several men from the civilian defence, so I went there to see if somebody could extend first aid to him." Mrs. Bajraktarevic, did you state this?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did state that. But I did it through that neighbour. She was the one who told me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What did this neighbour tell you?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: She said that there was that Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what is the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, it is 3.30 now. How much time do you think you'd still need? If it's more than just a couple of minutes, I'd suggest that we adjourn until tomorrow. But of course, I'm not aware of how much is still in your programme.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has envisaged quite a number of questions. We would like this witness to be shown some video material, and the circular photograph, number -- Prosecution Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I have to apologise. It seems to be Monday for me as well. We started at half past 2.00, so we usually continue until 4.00. I'm -- I don't know what bothers me, but please proceed. And, yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at any rate, I think I understood that we would have the possibility to state our position regarding the issue raised by Mr. Ierace at the end of the afternoon, so the Defence would like to be given between 5 and 10 minutes maximum in order to clarify its position regarding this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's fair. So Ms. Pilipovic, you've until that very moment, a little bit over a quarter of an hour, to go, so please proceed. And I apologise again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, can you tell us, please, what were those people wearing, the people that you went to see?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time see any member of the Civil Defence in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You are, therefore, telling us that it was from a neighbour that you learned that the people in question were members of the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many people there were?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you had gone to see the wife of the late Bosnic?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay at her place, can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I stayed enough to tell her that her husband had been wounded and that she should go to the hospital, if possible, to help him. That's all I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of the street where the Bosnic family lived?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but a moment ago, His Honour said that we should not be mentioning names and now you're asking me -- you have asked me even about my street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm now asking you about the street where the late Bosnic lived.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was Debelo Brdo, if it's not protected; I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if the police came, on that day or later, to see the Bosnic family?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the wife of the late Bosnic after that?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you used to see the wife of the late Sopi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: You mean when I saw her? When I went over to inform them, but I didn't have any specific contact with her. I didn't meet with her.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you used to see the wife of the late Bajram Sophie?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any contact with Bajram either.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that, after this incident - and you don't when this incident happened - you never saw the late Sopi Bajram?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you didn't see his wife either after that?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this point, the Defence would like to show to the witness the photograph number 3279S, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic. On the other hand, I have to rectify what I said before, or at least to change. We said the Defence would have 10 minutes at the end of the afternoon session. I have looked at the time spent. I expect you -- that you'd be able to conclude your cross-examination by 4.00, since you then used the same time as the Prosecution did. So for very practical reasons, we would rather prefer to continue and see whether you can conclude the cross-examination of the witness, and then start tomorrow morning first at 9.00 with the other issue raised by Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that we are, here in this courtroom, already familiar with the considerable flexibility of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it is shown again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, can you see this photograph? Is it in front Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of you?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No -- oh, yes, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The hills that we can see on the photograph above this -- above the car --

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Over there, well it's on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what area that is?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the transcript, perhaps it could be said that the image shown is a section of road with a white van parked alongside it. And having regard to the earlier evidence, the city of Sarajevo is behind the van. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, so you don't know the name of the hills that we can see above the road which you identified and the car which can be seen on the road?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I said that the road leads up to the area of Kula and Brajkovac. The road that we called Prasine.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you have just confirmed that this is the road leading up to Kula and Brajkovac?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the area of Kula was situated within the overall locality of Brajkovac?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is at the end of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that the portion of the road leading to Brajkovac and the area called Kula was under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. When you get to Kula, you turn left, leading towards Osmice. Like you said, there is the street, this road, which leads to Lukavica, yes. This is the same road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the BH army had its positions in Brajkovac?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I just told you, I never went there when there were troops there and when there was gunfire. The only occasions I went there was when I had to gather wood, firewood. We never dared go there. As for the village of Brajkovac, it was partly destroyed. The houses were torn down, even to this date, many people have not yet returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since you're telling us that there were some destroyed houses there, am I to understand that there was fighting in this area of the town?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why do you say that there was some destroyed houses there?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: It was later on that I went there. I have a friend who lives there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "later," what exactly do you mean? In what year did you go there?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: After the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your friends tell you that there had been fighting in the area and that the Bosnian troops were there?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't care to ask any such questions. These are not affairs of the women.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we move towards the right side of the photograph so that we can see the reservoir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that does not appear in this photograph. That's in the other photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you like to have the other one, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I apologise. I thought that it could be seen on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's 3279S.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 9S, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see on this photograph the location of the reservoir, where it used to be?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: As I said, it could have been a reservoir or just a construction site. I didn't go there. I don't know how it was exactly. But I know that there is a reservoir there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the reservoir in question was under the Bosnian Army control during the conflict in Sarajevo, and that it was the BH army soldiers who supervised it?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but I told you that there were no troops in the area. It is a civilian area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the reservoir was guarded by the BH army during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No. Civilians were there, people who used to work there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have water during the conflict, in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes we did; sometimes we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did this reservoir supply your neighbourhood? Was it used to supply your neighbourhood with water?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, not my neighbourhood. The so-called Bistrica, that is the name of the location where the water came that we had. It was the water from Bistrica that we got from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which part of the town was supplied with water from this reservoir?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course not. How would I know that? I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, during the examination-in-chief, you told us that you knew that in your neighbourhood and in the area of the town where you went to gather wood, firewood, that a woman by the name of Fadila was killed in that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what Fadila was doing at the time she was killed, as you said, and when that was, if you can tell us that, please?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: She was chopping wood on a log, and it was a foggy day. There was fog all around her. She didn't finish her work before the fog lifted. She continued with her work, despite that fact, and that's how a bullet found her, and it hit her in the stomach. I don't know how they managed to take off her clothes. She was simply dragged down to the area that we called Civare [phoen], from where she was taken to hospital where she eventually died.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, during the conflict, that is, during the war in Sarajevo in 1992, 1993, 1994, where exactly that incident took place, can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. Well, you know, if I had known that I would be here one day as a witness, I would have noted everything down. But I, of course, didn't know that. And I cannot -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, I would like to put to you that, in the statement that you gave on the 6th of May to the OTP investigators, on the page which ends with 351, that you described the event in question. I can read that out to you. "There was another woman, a neighbour, who was killed by a sniper. She went to the water to wash some clothes."

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: "I think her name was Fadila." Can you tell us, please, what information here is correct; what you stated in your statement or what you testified here before the Court?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's all the same. I didn't state anything different.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In response to a question by the Prosecution today, you said that she was chopping some firewood, whereas to the investigators you declared that she had gone to the water to wash some clothes.

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: First of all, Fadila, or Dila as they called her, she was chopping wood, firewood at the time. And this other woman, she had gone to the water to wash the clothes. She wanted to take some rest, and she got killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of this other woman, the one who went to the water to wash the clothes?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know her name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you tell the OTP investigators that her name was Fadila, then?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, there are two Fadilas; one of them was chopping the firewood, and the other one was washing the clothes. They are both called Fadila, or Dila.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you gave the statement to the OTP investigators, why didn't you tell them that there were two women by the name of Fadila?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If one looks at the statement, one will see in that same statement, the witness did refer to both women by name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then of course I have a problem since we do not have the statement. If, Ms. Pilipovic, you're still of the opinion that it's mentioned only once -- yes, I think under these special circumstances, the Chamber...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I hand up my copy. I've mark the two passages with a black cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your permission, what we read in the statement - I don't know whether you have the same one - is that there was a Fadila, the one we talked about -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know whether we have the same statement, but I think it's the one that ends with 652. What we read in the statement is that there was a woman whose name was Fadila, apparently she was hit with a bullet, and she had gone to the water to wash the clothes. This is the woman that we speak about, and not about the one that she went to chop wood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, first of all, I think that you have not asked permission to deal with the cross-examination together. But apart from that, Mr. Ierace is pointing at the sixth paragraph of page 651 as one of the incidents, and the other one, the passage you just indicated. The question was why the witness didn't talk about two women being killed. Mr. Ierace says that he should object against this question because she did refer to two different. Yes, Ms. Pilipovic. Is there anything you'd like to tell us in response? I mean, we just checked on whether there were two incidents. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour. Let me try to clarify this with a question to the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- whether the names Fadila and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the objection is against the question you put to the witness. That is, why she didn't tell about the second. That objection is sustained. So you can't ask that question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, can you please answer the following question: Is it true that Dila Peljto was killed in the shooting which was done by Serb soldiers, as you testified?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she was the one who was gathering firewood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, these two events, these two incidents, when did they take place?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: These two persons, were they acquaintances of yours? Did you know them?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How old were they, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: They were young. But I didn't meet with them on a regular basis. I didn't have any regular contact with them. They had moved to the area from some other place. I mean, they are not from Sarajevo. And that is the reason why I'm not very familiar with --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So your testimony is that you had only heard about this incident, that you did not actually eyewitness this incident -- or rather, these incidents when these women were killed?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you only heard about these two incidents?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: See, it was impossible for me to see the location where they were killed. Had I been able to see the location, it means that I would have been killed, too. I was in the vicinity, and I could see this Peljto woman being dragged to hospital. That is something that I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, your son who was a member of the army and who was wounded, where was he wounded? In which part of the town?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: On the opposite side from where we lived, in the area of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that your son was taking part in fighting when he was wounded?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know really.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This concludes our cross-examination of the witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pilipovic. It is 4.00, but I wonder whether there's any need to re-examine the witness, Mr. Ierace? And how much time that would take, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is only one issue which may be dealt with perhaps in one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at the interpreters' booth, I wanted to stop a half an hour too early. Five minutes extra, would that be acceptable?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, we'll do it, Your Honour. But the interference is very bad indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's see whether we can finish. Please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, you were asked a question about the road to Brajkovac and Kula. In particular, you were asked who controlled that road. Which of the armed forces controlled that road?

utterances.speaker: NURA BAJRAKTAREVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Bajraktarevic, you've answered all the questions of both parties, of the Prosecution and the Defence. The Judges have no additional questions to you. That means that this concludes your testimony for this Court. We thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We thank you very much for having --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You know how it is. My husband is sick, and I left him. He has been all alone all day today. I don't know how he's doing really. I didn't expect to stay so long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And at least I'm glad that we could conclude your testimony today. I thank you very much for coming and giving your testimony. And a good and, I hope, a quick trip home again to your husband. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, let's just see whether we can finish with the exhibits, the documents, which are not documents but videos and electronic photos. Am I right that we have seen today video P3280S; we have seen 360-degrees photograph, 3279S; and another 360-degrees photograph from a different position, 3279SS.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that the Defence is objecting against the 360-degrees photographs. I take it the objection is also valid here. And you also know how this Chamber decides on these kind of objections. So then they are admitted into evidence. We have another document which has been shown to the Chamber in response to an objection made to one of the questions. It is a witness statement which I think should be marked for identification. It bears the ERN numbers 0203-0650, next page ending with 51, third page ending with 52, then another page, 53, and finally, page 54. Mr. Ierace, I noticed that you, apart from the markings you made, especially in support of your objections, these are the black Xs, there are also some red linings or stripes in it. I don't know whether you would prefer to take a new copy or that you would leave it just as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have a clean copy that I could mark in the same fashion with black crosses. So perhaps I could change the one you have for another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll mark it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that there's any objection. Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We do not have a statement marked that way in English. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no marking. Just in order to indicate the two spots where the witness talks about the first incident, that is, the incident with Dila Peljto, that's the witness statement, the sixth paragraph on page 652, it's just a cross. Mr. Ierace, if you've marked one, I'll perhaps return this one to you. Have a look at it, and then show it to the Defence so that I have not -- it's not necessary to explain everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm happy for the Defence to see both, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course you could give them. We would like to see the second one first. If you perhaps first give the other one already to the Defence, and then the copy replacing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not know whether I can interfere, but this is a document in English. The Defence will accept the admission of this document, but without any marks or regardless of the colour by anybody at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, it's not a question of admitting this document in evidence. It's a matter of marking for identification. This document has been given to the Chamber with the -- I would say the black marking is relevant in it, that it's two Xs, indicating those areas in the statement where the two incidents described and, I would say, ignored in questioning the witness are indicated. That's the document as it is shown to the Chamber and I think, as such, it should be marked for identification because that's the -- but I would rather leave out the red stripes. Madam Registrar, then, this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will gladly first give it to you so that you see it is exactly the same, apart from the red stripes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have full confidence in the Chamber, and you know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then, Madam Registrar, this document should be marked for identification. I don't know exactly at what number we are.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was provided by the Prosecution with identification number MFI-12. Or shall I say identification number 12. Sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think then we have had everything dealt with which we should deal with. That means that -- yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, earlier today you pointed out -- you said, rather, that the Prosecution had not notified the technical section of our intention to show a video. I do apologise for that. We had handed a letter to the registrar last Wednesday, the 13th of March, indicating both the witnesses to be called this week and also the exhibits, including the video. I had not realised there was any further requirement upon us to indicate to the technical people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I understand, especially also if both a video should be shown and a computer 360-degrees photograph, that they need to prepare this. Of course, I accept your apologies. And perhaps for both parties, if there are high-tech facilities needed, please make sure - I'm not saying that they are not on the list of your exhibits - but please make sure that everyone is well aware of what we need in order to prepare it. Because we had a lot of technical facilities, both face distortion and computer evidence and video, and that takes a lot of lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There will be another video to be shown, not by the next witness, but the witness after. Perhaps I could indicate that at this stage. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I assume that the technical booth took notice of that. I see you're nodding. Then I thank everyone for giving the opportunity to Mrs. Bajraktarevic to finish her testimony today, although it took us 12 minutes extra. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, The Hague time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 4.11 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of March, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
